### 2. What was wrong, and the source facts that settle it

The locator comment I authored claimed two things that the source contradicts:

- "the candidates are always ancestors of the start and never the start" — **false**;
- "the start itself is reachable only at `--skip=0`, which no caller asks for" — **false**.

The facts: `data parse_verdict_restore_ancestor_ordinals: List<Int> = [0, 1, ..., 11]`
(`dag/gunbc/parse_verdict_schema.dag`), one locate row per ordinal, and each row runs
`git rev-list --first-parent --skip=<ordinal> --max-count=1 "$BASE_SHA"` (`.github/workflows/witnesses.yml`, the
locate step). `--skip=0 --max-count=1 X` prints `X`, so ordinal 0 IS the start. Nothing in this code enforces the
exclusion of the judged commit; whether it can appear is a consequence of which commit each route names as its
start. The job's checkout is `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` with `fetch-depth: 0` (`witnesses.yml:38`).

### 3. The correction, as it now reads

```
// THE LOCATOR: the first-parent history of a START commit, newest first, at the declared ordinals, each written
// as a step output which the restore keys and the record step read. These are selection facts about event
// metadata, not a relaxation of anything: what a receipt stands on is decided per member by
// gunbc.parse_verdict_schema .parse_verdict_standing from the head's parse-compiler identity, the base's
// identity, and the line built from the digest THIS walk recomputed from the bytes on disk. An ancestor's
// position in this list confers no standing; it chooses which published entry the cache hands back, and it is
// reported in the counts line.
//
// The start comes from parse_verdict_ancestor_base_sha_expr: github.event.pull_request.base.sha when
// github.event_name is pull_request, otherwise github.event.before -- so a default-branch push starts at the
// commit main held before this event, and the merge_group and workflow_dispatch triggers name no start at all,
// where every ordinal is a typed miss and the walk is a full walk. The list is
// `git rev-list --first-parent --skip=<ordinal> --max-count=1 <start>` over the declared ordinals 0..11, so
// ordinal 0 IS the start itself and ordinals 1..11 are its first-parent predecessors.
//
// NOTHING HERE EXCLUDES THE COMMIT UNDER VERIFICATION, and this code enforces no such exclusion: whether the
// judged commit can appear depends entirely on which commit the event names as the start. On a pull request the
// start is the base sha the event reports, which is not the commit this job verifies -- the job checks out
// github.sha, GitHub's merge commit for the pull_request triggers, distinct from the source head
// github.event.pull_request.head.sha; nothing requires the reported base to be an ancestor of either. On a push
// the start is github.event.before, and a force push can make it a commit that is not an ancestor of
// github.sha at all, while a batched push (several commits in one event) neither makes the two equal nor by
// itself fails anything. No behaviour under those event shapes has been executed here: this paragraph is a
// reading of the workflow source and the emitted YAML.
//
// The script is a bash node tree emitted through bash_emit, as the release-bins runners are; no shell is
// authored here.
```

Three things this deliberately does NOT do: it adds no `git merge-base --is-ancestor` guard (that option stays
listed for decision, not assumed away); it claims no waiver of the receipt standing contract, and puts that
contract first; and it claims nothing has been executed under any of those event shapes. One addition beyond the
minimum wording, flagged rather than smuggled: naming `merge_group` and `workflow_dispatch` as triggers that name
no start, so their walk is a full walk — the completion of the statement "PR start is `event.pull_request.base.sha`
and push start is `event.before`", without which a reader could infer those triggers reuse something.

### 7. Extraction and verification recipe (exact)

`comment.md` is the raw body as stored by GitHub, e.g.
`gh api repos/gunb-ai/gunbc/issues/comments/COMMENT_ID --jq .body > comment.md`.

```
extract() { awk -v s="$1" '$0=="GZB64-BEGIN "s{f=1;next} $0=="GZB64-END "s{f=0} f' comment.md | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d | gzip -dc; }

extract section-5-commit-object > commit.raw
sha256sum commit.raw                                  # 9ba15f8445a58986475ea6440a07e59719ed8a6dfe41b16da50e28941402a09a
git hash-object -t commit --stdin < commit.raw         # bda8255e415bf924e0bf941f8538f2ddec4c1770

extract section-6-p5-to-p7 > p5_to_p7.patch
sha256sum p5_to_p7.patch                               # 0c42baf23a8fc861cb7e233c9cc46542d1661506bb119f673fa7121a754d169d
grep '^diff --git' p5_to_p7.patch                      # exactly 3 files: dag/gunbc/parse_verdict_restore.dag,
                                                       # src/v2/cli/population_verbs.dag, src/v2/test/claim/cli/population_verbs.dag
grep -E '^[+-]' p5_to_p7.patch | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | sed 's/^.//' | grep -vE '^\s*(//|$)' | wc -l   # 0

extract section-6-cumulative-patch > cum.patch
sha256sum cum.patch                                    # 777ae6561298ff0f88e9a694ec35f7a7d929f96b4fbd855934fef5a28c66e0b0
git clone --no-checkout <repo-url> scratch && cd scratch
git fetch -q origin ed007978dc2a67096df619b1b91566458dfb2ffd && git checkout -q ed007978dc2a
git apply --check cum.patch && git apply cum.patch
git add -A && git write-tree                           # 96103c723b4c5096142c50847bd18b3d14020e9a
```
